note: SH1043 — what the console costs to load, before the first row of content. Read by test/console-size-budget.test.mjs against a built ../shio-app/src/main/resources/public, and printed by `pnpm --filter shio-react run size`. Raise a ceiling deliberately and say why in the commit, the way token-budgets.properties has governed the agent's cost since SH113: this is the same rule for the half of the product a person waits for.
seed: SH1043 seeded this at 7473483 raw / 2200187 gzip, and SH1044 spent that number the same day: deleting vite.config.ts's `manualChunks` took it to 1542579 raw / 413169 gzip, because the rule written to keep GraphiQL out of the eager bundle was what put it there. Four entries went with it — vendor-graphiql.js, vendor-graphiql.css, vendor-codemirror.js and vendor-lib.js are no longer eager, and this gate fails on a ceiling that outlives its chunk, which is how they came to be deleted here rather than left as numbers nobody was measuring. The ceilings carry ~5% of room for the reason SH736 gives one gate over: a ceiling set to the measurement refuses the next change instead of measuring it.
raised: SH1046 raised the eager ceilings and index.js's, and the reason is the whole of what this file is for: adopting `@tanstack/react-query` cost 32894 raw / 10054 gzip, measured here before and after, against seventeen catalogue reads that each refetched a whole collection on every mount. That is the trade this gate exists to make visible — 2.4% of the gzipped load for a folder-to-folder walk that stops refetching the post-type catalogue per folder. Nothing else moved: index.css, breadcrumb.context.js and rolldown-runtime.js are byte-identical across the change. SH1056 raised the two eager ceilings again, by 7000 raw / 2000 gzip: the site editor's Languages section, the translations menu's narrowing and the rules both read cost 6871 raw / 1854 gzip, all of it index.js, measured by building the tree with and without them (1583519 → 1590390 raw, 425245 → 427099 gzip). That took the raw room to 3.9% of the ceiling, under the 4% the headroom check asks for; the raise restores it without touching index.js's own ceiling, which still has 44 KB under it. SH1060 raised them again, by 6000 raw / 2000 gzip: SH1058's out-of-date marker in the translations menu and SH1060's Languages board cost 5873 raw / 1349 gzip together, measured on the same build before and after (1590390 → 1596263 raw, 427099 → 428448 gzip). The board is a screen a curator opens when a site has more than one language, and it is the first console surface that turns the translation backlog into a work list; index.js's own ceiling is untouched and still has 37 KB under it. SH1061's side-by-side workspace measured 4326 raw / 950 gzip on top of that (1596263 → 1600589 raw), and the raw ceiling went 1668000 -> 1674000 with it: at 1668000 the fit was 700 bytes, which is a ceiling that refuses the next addition rather than measuring it — SH736's lesson, and the reason every raise here leaves room. SH1065 raised the gzip ceiling alone, 449000 -> 452000, and the reason is the headroom rule rather than a feature: reading the server's own Content-Disposition on the site download — so a zip saved from the console and one written by `shio export` are the same file instead of two names for one artifact — measured under 100 gzip bytes (1568.0 -> 1568.1 KB raw, 420.9 KB gzip on both builds), and it was those bytes that took the room from 18,010 to 17,950 against the 17,960 the 4% check asks for. A raise of 3000 puts the room back to 4.6% rather than to the measurement, which is the same lesson every entry above records: a ceiling at the total refuses the next change instead of measuring it. The raw ceiling is untouched and still has 106 KB under it, which is why only one of the two moved. SH1088 raised nothing: taking design system 2026.3.12 moved the eager total from 1568.1 to 1570.3 KB raw and 420.9 to 423.0 KB gzip, inside both ceilings, but regrouped the chunks. breadcrumb.context.js is no longer emitted, and index.es.js (397.6 KB raw, 126.4 KB gzip) carries the package's ES entry with the React runtime it shares, while index.js fell to 924 KB. The entry was renamed to the chunk that now exists, with ~5% room. The +2.2 KB raw left the eager raw room at 66,013 bytes against the 66,960 the 4% check asks for, so the raw ceiling went 1674000 -> 1680000 (4.3% room), for the same reason SH1065 moved the gzip one: a ceiling at the total refuses the next change instead of measuring it. The gzip ceiling did not move. SH964 raised the eager raw ceiling 1680000 -> 1700000, the eager gzip ceiling 452000 -> 460000 and index.es.js to 443000 raw / 141000 gzip: mounting VigletAssistant as the status dock cost 14.6 KB raw / 5.3 KB gzip, all of it index.es.js, measured by building with and without it (eager 1572.0 -> 1586.6 KB raw, 423.6 -> 429.0 KB gzip; index.es.js 397.6 -> 411.9 KB raw). Loading it with lazy() was measured too and saved nothing: the bundler keeps the design system's whole ES entry in one shared eager chunk, so the component lands there whichever way it is imported. The raises restore ~4.4% of room on both totals and ~5% on the chunk. SH969 raised the eager raw ceiling 1700000 -> 1712000 for the headroom rule rather than one feature: the dock work after SH964's raise (SH966's report store and refusal reporter, SH968's run tracker and shared stream, SH969's schedule reports and replay) took the eager load from 1586.6 to 1594.0 KB raw, leaving 66.2 KB of room against the 68 KB the 4% check asks for. The new ceiling leaves 4.7%. The same work took the eager gzip total to 431.7 KB against 449.2 KB, 3.9% of room, so the gzip ceiling went 460000 -> 466000 (5.1%). Every chunk ceiling is untouched. SH988 raised the eager raw ceiling 1712000 -> 1724000 for the headroom rule: SH971's dock preferences dialog, SH972's editor dock and SH988's version rail, diff and inline review diff took the eager load from 1594.0 to 1606.4 KB raw, leaving 65.5 KB of room against the 66.9 KB the 4% check asks for. The new ceiling leaves 4.7%; the gzip ceiling and every chunk ceiling are untouched. SH1006 raised the eager gzip ceiling 466000 -> 472000 for the headroom rule: SH988's created-page panel and field restore and SH1006's chat store, relay hook and send took the eager gzip total to 437.4 KB against 455.1 KB, 3.9% of room against the 4% the check asks for. The new ceiling leaves 5.1%; the raw ceiling and every chunk ceiling are untouched. SH1019 raised the eager raw ceiling 1724000 -> 1736000 for the headroom rule: the dock chat, its change actions and a field's ask-the-agent dialog (SH1006, SH1007, SH1019) took the eager raw total from 1606.4 to 1616.4 KB, leaving 67.1 KB of room against the 67.3 KB the 4% check asks for. The new ceiling leaves 4.8%; the gzip ceiling and every chunk ceiling are untouched. SH1026 raised the eager raw ceiling 1736000 -> 1800000 and the eager gzip ceiling 472000 -> 490000: drawing the browser's table view with the design system's BentoDataTable, which brings the virtualised body, sortable headers and column picker the task asks for, took the eager load from 1627.9 to 1671.1 KB raw and 442.0 to 454.9 KB gzip (1711147 / 465774 bytes), all of it index.js and index.es.js, measured by building HEAD and the change. Loading the table with lazy() was measured as well and cost more, 1673.5 KB raw, because the package's bento entry is one module: the component lands in the eager shared chunk either way, and the dynamic import only regrouped the rest into four differently named chunks. The raises leave 4.9% of room on both totals; every chunk ceiling is untouched and index.js still has 155 KB under it. SH1090 raised the eager raw ceiling 1800000 -> 1865000 and the eager gzip ceiling 490000 -> 510000: moving the console from <BrowserRouter> to a data router (createBrowserRouter and RouterProvider), which is what useBlocker needs to stop an in-app navigation away from unsaved work, cost 55191 raw / 17130 gzip, all of it index.js, measured by building HEAD (1725793 / 469409) and the change (1780984 / 486539). The ladder had no cheaper rung: React Router 7 offers a blocker only on a data router, and a hand-rolled one would patch history underneath the router it does not own. The raises leave 4.5% of room on both totals; index.js's own ceiling is untouched and still has 87 KB under it. SH1024 and SH1026 raised the eager raw ceiling 1865000 -> 1880000 and the eager gzip ceiling 510000 -> 514000 for the headroom rule: the filter bar on the trash and the review queue, the agent option, the facet counts, saved views on four lists, grid thumbnails and the windowed list and grid took the eager load from 1780984 to 1790679 raw and 486539 to 489619 gzip, measured on a build of the tree, leaving 72.6 KB of raw room against the 72.9 KB the 4% check asks for and 20 gzip bytes over its line. The raises leave 4.7% on both; every chunk ceiling is untouched. SH1116 raised the eager raw ceiling 1880000 -> 1900000 and the gzip ceiling 514000 -> 520000, and the reason is mostly not SH1116: its own five-page migration to the query layer measured **1.3 KB raw / 0.2 KB gzip**, taken by building HEAD (1766.7 KB raw / 483.2 KB gzip) and the change (1768.0 / 483.4) on the same tree. What actually tripped the headroom check is that this was the first run measured against a build made *from the tree under test*: the eager total had reached 1810450 raw / 495034 gzip, leaving 3.70% and 3.69% of room against the 4% this gate asks for, and every green run before it had measured whatever build happened to be sitting in `resources/public` — which is SH1126 by name, the open task for a gate that measures bytes that may be older than the change. So the raise records accumulated growth that a stale build was hiding rather than a feature's cost, and it leaves 4.71% and 4.80%. Reading this entry as "the query layer cost 20 KB" would be wrong by a factor of fifteen. SH1180 raised the eager ceilings 1900000 -> 1975000 raw and 520000 -> 542000 gzip, and index.es.js's 443000 -> 485000 raw and 141000 -> 154000 gzip, for one measured cause: SH1094's BentoSplitPage, whose drag divider is react-resizable-panels (the data-group, data-panel and data-separator attributes in the chunk). Building each of the day's commits on the same tree put it at SH1094 alone: index.es.js 426480 -> 461335 raw (+34855), with SH971, SH1082, SH1148 and SH1178 adding nothing to it. It lands in index.es.js because the design system's Resizable wrapper lives in its root entry, which is the shared eager chunk, so a lazy page would move nothing (SH964 measured the same for the assistant). SH1094 itself shipped unmeasured: the gate correctly skipped a build from another tree on every run that touched the console, and the first run that did not was SH1091's. The eager total is now 1880166 raw / 516000 gzip; the raises leave 4.8% on both, and index.es.js 4.9% raw / 4.6% gzip.

index.js.why: the console itself plus the shared vendor code the bundler folded in once `manualChunks` stopped hand-placing it: React, the router, the query layer (SH1046) and the libraries every route needs

index.css.why: Tailwind's output plus the design system's own sheet

index.es.js.why: the design system's ES entry and the React runtime it shares with the console, which the bundler emits as one eager chunk since 2026.3.11 (SH1088); it replaced breadcrumb.context.js, and index.js shrank by what it took; since SH1094 it also carries react-resizable-panels, the divider BentoSplitPage draws with, about 35 KB raw (SH1180)

rolldown-runtime.js.why: the bundler's own module runtime, which every other chunk is loaded through
